persona.role: PhD student and machine learning researcher
current_work: Running a pilot study on uncertainty calibration with noisy target prevalence estimates
Maintaining research code and experiment infrastructure
Analyzing the first results from the new calibration pilot
Reading and synthesizing literature on uncertainty calibration
priorities: Run the predefined minimal pilot without expanding its design prematurely
Determine whether calibration degradation under prevalence-estimation noise is measurable and stable
Document unexpected results and distinguish implementation issues from substantive effects
Use the first pilot results to decide whether a larger experiment is justified

circumstances: The researcher runs the minimal pilot defined on Day 23 across the predefined prevalence-noise levels. The run completes, but the effect is not monotonic: moderate noise produces a larger calibration degradation than the highest noise level. The researcher checks whether this comes from a coding or metric issue, verifies the perturbation statistics, and finds that the observed non-monotonicity is real under the current setup. They inspect per-class results and discover that the aggregate metric hides opposite behavior across classes. Rather than immediately expanding to more datasets, they document the finding and define one targeted diagnostic for the next day. A short unrelated browsing detour occurs during a long experiment-monitoring window.

activities.title: Run the minimal prevalence-noise pilot
activities.summary: The researcher verified the fixed pilot configuration, launched the experiment across predefined prevalence-noise levels, waited for completion, and loaded the resulting metrics. The pilot completed without execution errors.
activities.context: First substantive run of the pilot designed and smoke-tested on Day 23.

activities.title: Investigate the non-monotonic pilot result
activities.summary: The aggregate calibration metric did not worsen monotonically with increasing prevalence-estimation noise. The researcher checked uncertainty intervals, perturbation statistics, raw predictions, aggregation paths, and metric definitions. The pattern persisted after direct recomputation.
activities.context: Unexpected result from the first substantive pilot run.

activities.title: Inspect class-level calibration behavior
activities.summary: The researcher decomposed the aggregate result by class and prevalence regime and found opposite class-level changes that partly cancel in the aggregate metric. The observation was recorded as a possible explanation for the non-monotonic aggregate pattern.
activities.context: Follow-up to the validated non-monotonic aggregate result.

activities.title: Define a bounded diagnostic follow-up
activities.summary: After a brief unrelated product-browsing detour and a break, the researcher outlined one class-level calibration diagnostic, prepared analysis cells without executing them, and recorded constraints for the next run. Broader experiments were left unplanned.
activities.context: Turning an unexpected pilot result into one targeted diagnostic rather than expanding the experiment matrix.

key_observations: The first substantive pilot completed successfully, but aggregate calibration did not degrade monotonically as prevalence-estimation noise increased.
The non-monotonic pattern survived checks of the perturbation distribution, raw predictions, aggregation path, and metric implementation.
Class-level analysis showed opposite changes that partly cancel in the aggregate metric, giving a plausible but not yet established explanation for the aggregate behavior.
The researcher converted the unexpected result into one bounded diagnostic rather than immediately adding datasets, noise models, or seeds.
No broader conclusion about the hypothesis is justified from the single pilot run.
priority_alignment: The predefined pilot was run before expanding the design.
Analysis focused on determining whether the surprising result was computational or substantive.
The next step remains narrowly tied to interpreting the first pilot rather than launching a larger benchmark.
important_uncertainty: It is unclear whether the class-level pattern is stable across another seed or is specific to this pilot run.
The current aggregate metric may obscure behavior that is scientifically important at the class level.
The pilot does not yet establish whether noisy prevalence estimates consistently affect calibration in the hypothesized direction.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Run the single predefined class-conditional diagnostic, preferably with the same pilot configuration and one additional seed only if needed to determine whether the observed class-level pattern is stable.

primary_action.title: Run the class-level diagnostic
primary_action.reason: The pilot produced a surprising but internally consistent aggregate result, and one targeted diagnostic can distinguish aggregate cancellation from a more general class-conditional effect.

secondary_action.title: Keep the follow-up bounded
secondary_action.reason: The current evidence supports one diagnostic, not a larger experiment matrix.

things_not_to_do: Do not add multiple datasets or noise models before interpreting the first pilot.
Do not assume the non-monotonic result is a bug after the direct recomputation checks passed.
Do not treat the class-level explanation as established from one run.
Do not optimize the aggregate metric at the expense of inspecting class-conditional behavior.
